**Observation Log:**

- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/21 (Sun) 16:44
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Section 13 of the text outlines the relationship of the current Act to other laws.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] It specifies that nothing in the Act is meant to affect other laws, regulations, or authorities, except as expressly provided.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Act provides that the President or the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States (CFIUS) can still exercise any authority under the Defense Production Act of 1950.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Secretary cannot review a transaction involving the acquisition of an information and communications technology product or service by a United States person if it is authorized under a United States government-industrial security program or for meeting a national security or law enforcement requirement.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Section 14 of the act states that all administrative actions, including delegations, rules, regulations, orders, determinations, licenses made by the Secretary under Executive Order 13873 and the International Emergency Economic Powers Act shall continue in effect according to their terms.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] These actions will remain effective as if made under the authority of this Act until modified, superseded, set aside, or revoked under the authority of this Act.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] This continuation is without regard to any restrictions or limitations under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] This section includes several miscellaneous provisions.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Paperwork Reduction Act will not apply to any actions taken by the Secretary to implement the bill.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Secretary may appoint candidates directly to positions without regard to certain provisions of the U.S. Code.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The functions exercised under the bill are not subject to certain sections of the U.S. Code, except for civil penalties imposed under section 9(b).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Protected information in civil actions challenging actions or findings under the bill shall be submitted ex parte and in camera to the court and maintained under seal.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The use of information provisions of certain sections of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978 shall not apply in a civil action brought under this bill.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The bill does not create a right to obtain access to information in the possession of the Federal Government or prohibit, mitigate, or take action against a covered transaction or interest.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Any information submitted to the Federal Government in accordance with the bill is exempt from disclosure under the Freedom of Information Act.
